PASS: PASS, gate 1, audit of ace1897.

Sprint file: read fresh. Unchanged since start (12574c0 is the only commit touching it).

Handoff: read at the audited commit. It has a Round 1 section quoting VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0, with 595 tests.

My own check: npm run verify at ace1897, on a clean tree. Result: verify=0, VERIFY PASS exit=0, 52 test files and 595 tests passed.

- R1 Met. lib/site-title.ts holds SITE_TITLE and datedTitle, joined with one ASCII space. A grep for the site name in app and lib outside tests finds only that file's constant, plus comments. The only metadata title fields in the app are the layout (SITE_TITLE) and the two generateMetadata functions (datedTitle). A unit test covers 1969-07-20.
- R2 Met. The date page's generateMetadata uses only parseDatePageParam, isAfterToday and datedTitle. The module imports createAnonClient for the page body, but the metadata function never calls it, and a test asserts neither Supabase nor fetch is called. I read the acceptance criterion as covering the metadata's own dependencies, not the page module's. Invalid, out-of-range and future dates return an empty object, so they keep the default title and never show a future date.
- R3 Met. The get_reading_by_id lookup moved verbatim into app/reading/[id]/load.ts as loadReadingById, wrapped in React cache(). The classification is unchanged: unavailable is logged once, and 22P02 or empty is notFound. Both the page and generateMetadata call it.
  The test mocks cache() as a per-test memo, because Vitest loads React's client build, where cache does not memoize. Dev Team showed the test fails with a pass-through cache. The production-build evidence (the stand-in's RPC log) shows exactly 1 get_reading_by_id call per request for found, unknown and malformed ids.
- R4 Met. Unknown and malformed ids and an outage return an empty object. Redirect routes set no metadata. error.tsx sets none.
  The new app/not-found.tsx removes Next's built-in "404: This page could not be found." title, which pre-dates this sprint, from route-level 404s. It is a copy of Next 16.3's fallback markup without the title tag. Before-and-after screenshots are byte-identical by sha256 in both colour schemes. The handoff states the 404 status and the noindex tag are unaffected.
  The constant CSS string through dangerouslySetInnerHTML is static, with no input, so it raises no injection concern.
- R5 Met. description is unchanged in the layout, and the banner and date band are untouched.
- R6 Met. Tests cover R1, R2 (valid and refused dates), R3 (found, unknown, 22P02, outage, and one-read sharing), and the 404 page having no title tag.
- R7 Met.

Routed to Master Controller: the handoff says the user decided, during the build, to add app/not-found.tsx, which the sprint file does not name. I have no record of that decision other than the handoff. Master Controller should record it in the sprint file, or in decisions, so it is durable. That includes the trade-off that this copy keeps Next 16.3's look if a later Next version changes its 404. It is in service of R4 and changes nothing visible, so it is not scope creep and not a finding.

Still UNOWNED, with Master Controller: the 3 lint warnings in the sprint 45 and 46 probe scripts. No decision is on record yet.

For LiveQA:
- Step 1's grep also prints the chart's SVG title elements. The page title is the first one, in the head.
- On step 4, check document.title in the browser, not only curl. The built-in 404 title appeared only in the browser before this sprint.
commit=ace1897 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for ace18974b07127e386ce04e0ac693565ecc44703 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 1). LiveQA steps 1 to 5 pass on production. Step 6: GA4 Realtime was not watched, but the page_view hits sent to GA4 were captured, and their page title (dt) carries the date. No defects.

Tested 2026-11-25, about 16:16 to 16:20 UTC, against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.
Shipped commit ace1897. Production serves the pushed tip 39e2e2f: /api/health/db reports status ok, connected true, commit 39e2e2f, with migrationVersion unchanged at 20261122152710_navigation_exact_date_readings. git diff ace1897 origin/main touches only sprint docs, registry.json, and docs/sprints/state/sprint-49.json.
Tools: curl; headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) at 1280x900, and 390x900 (isMobile, hasTouch).
Note: the step 6 run sent real GA4 hits to G-NFY3Q9KSXH around 16:18 UTC, from headless Chromium.

STEP 1, /date/1969-07-20: PASS. curl, grep for the title tag: "<title>Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-20</title>" (the first match, in head). In the browser, document.title is "Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-20" at both widths.

STEP 2, navigation: PASS. A window marker set on load survived each navigation, and no document navigation request fired, so these were client-side with no reload:
- Previous day: "Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-19".
- Next day: "Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-20".
- Notable link to 1969-07-20: "Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-20".
- Random link: "Retroactive Horoscope 1963-11-24" (desktop) and "Retroactive Horoscope 1989-11-09" (phone).
- Banner home: "Retroactive Horoscope 2026-11-25".
- History back: the previous date's title.
At both widths, each title matched the date band (h1) after the navigation.
The date picker (filled 1912-04-15, then Go) gives "Retroactive Horoscope 1912-04-15". The picker is a GET form, so it's a full document load (2 document requests: /date?date= and its 307), which is the existing behaviour, not a client-side navigation.

STEP 3, /reading/<id>: PASS.
- /reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d: "Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-20" (curl and browser; date band "20 July 1969").
- /reading/9bd536d1-243f-49e7-8c59-af75b6d76067: "Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-21" (date band "21 July 1969").

STEP 4, plain title on 404s: PASS. curl and document.title both give "Retroactive Horoscope" for:
- /date/2024-02-30 (404);
- /date/not-a-date (404);
- /reading/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 (404);
- /reading/not-a-uuid (404);
- /no-such-page (404).
The built-in "404: This page could not be found." browser title no longer appears. The 404 page still looks like the built-in one: "404 This page could not be found.", h1 24px. Screenshot: s49_date_2024_02_30.png.

STEP 5, /: PASS. The redirect lands on /date/2026-11-25 (today, UTC), titled "Retroactive Horoscope 2026-11-25" (curl -L and browser).

STEP 6, GA4: Realtime NOT WATCHED. The captured page_view hits to www.google-analytics.com/g/collect carry:
- dl=/date/1969-07-20, dt "Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-20";
- dl=/date/1969-07-19, dt "Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-19" (after Previous day, client-side);
- dl=/date/1969-07-20, dt "Retroactive Horoscope 1969-07-20" (after Next day);
- dl=/date/2024-02-30, dt "Retroactive Horoscope".
So the title GA4 receives includes the date, and follows client-side navigation.
Sprint 46 regression check on the new 404 page: gtm.js loaded once on the 404 document (2 loads for 2 documents), and its page_view was sent.

R5: the description meta is unchanged ("Pick a date to see the sky over it and what happened that day, and have a horoscope written for it."). Its text in app/layout.tsx is identical at 78fd732 and ace1897. The banner and date band are unchanged.
0 page errors.
